- When sentiment is high (≥0.7), model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes; cap forecast peak at 2–3% below true peak in 30d horizon.  
- Model shows lag in mean reversion: if 18d history shows strong trend, forecast should align with 3–5d moving average of true values.  
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 3–5 days, reduce forecast slope for next 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.6→0.8→0.9), model often overshoots; apply 1–2% downward correction to 30d forecast.  
- If true outcome is >70% of 30d forecast, model is underestimating; increase forecast by 2–4% for next 10 days.  
- If sentiment is stable or declining, model tends to underestimate; apply 1–3% upward bias to forecast.
